compiled_state.title: ticket_reducer: STATUS fork tie-break uses parent pointer instead of event UUID -> non-deterministic resolution for concurrent siblings
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

process_status() in _processors.py uses data['parent_status_uuid'] (the parent pointer of incoming event) as the tie-break value, and stores it back in state['parent_status_uuid']. For real concurrent siblings — two STATUS events with the same parent — both have identical parent pointers, so the tie-break always resolves to 'incoming wins' regardless of event UUID ordering. This is non-deterministic (depends on replay order).

## Fix Direction

- Compare event['uuid'] values for the tie-break instead of data['parent_status_uuid']
- Advance state['parent_status_uuid'] to the winning event's own UUID (not its parent pointer)
- Update unit tests in test_processors.py to assert on event UUID semantics

## Source

Identified via Copilot PR review comments on PR #25 (lines 85, 113 of _processors.py).
